dedupe_keys.name: nsw level crossings on public roads 1 307 railway level crossings with control type rail owner and risk attributes alcam

description: An open dataset of railway level crossings on public roads in New South Wales, Australia. Contents: crossings currently documented in the Australian Level Crossing Assessment Model (ALCAM) database, based on information from road and rail managers and external contractors. The CSV read on 29 September 2026 held 1,307 rows, each with road name, location, line section, rail km, control type (858 passive, 449 active), control category (stop signs, give way signs, flashing lights, boom gates and flashing lights, rail operated gates), number of tracks, ALCAM rank, queuing, short stacking, sighting and conformity to Australian standards fields, suburb, local government area and rail owner (ARTC 646, UGL Regional Linx 573, Sydney Trains 40, V/Line 26 and others). Producer: Transport for NSW; the OpenStreetMap wiki also records it as the source of a MapRoulette import of missing level crossings. Coverage: New South Wales. Format and access: XLSX, CSV, GeoJSON, JSON, KML and shapefile downloads plus a PDF description and an interactive map on the NSW open data portal; free. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution. Caveats: 153 rows carry a location flag of no road and 30 have no flag, so positions need checking; the status and comments columns are empty; last modified March 2025. Simulation uses: exposure and safety analysis of rail-road interfaces, and level-crossing closure effects on road network models. Related records: none identified.
